history.q: Which Ottoman sultan conquered Constantinople in 1453?
history.fact: Mehmed was just 21 when the city fell, earning him the title Fatih, "the Conqueror."

history.q: Who was the first President of the Republic of Turkey?
history.fact: The surname Atatürk, meaning "Father of the Turks," was granted to him by parliament in 1934.

history.q: Which ancient city, the setting of Homer's Iliad, lies in northwest Anatolia?
history.fact: Heinrich Schliemann began excavating the mound of Hisarlık in 1871; the mound holds the remains of nine successive cities.

history.q: Which Ottoman sultan, known in Europe as "the Magnificent", reigned from 1520 to 1566?
history.fact: In Turkey he is called Kanuni, "the Lawgiver," for his overhaul of the empire's legal system.

history.q: Which Roman emperor refounded Byzantium as his new capital in 330 CE?
history.fact: The city was named Constantinople after him and remained an imperial capital for more than 1,500 years.

history.q: In what year was the Republic of Turkey proclaimed?
history.fact: The Republic was declared on 29 October 1923, now celebrated every year as Republic Day.

history.q: The Ottoman Empire takes its name from which founder?
history.fact: Osman led a small principality in northwest Anatolia around 1300; his dynasty ruled for over 600 years.

history.q: Which First World War campaign of 1915 saw Ottoman forces repel Allied landings on a peninsula by the Dardanelles?
history.fact: Mustafa Kemal rose to prominence as a commander there; Australia and New Zealand remember the campaign on Anzac Day.

history.q: Which Byzantine emperor ordered the great codification of Roman law known as the Corpus Juris Civilis?
history.fact: Justinian's law code became the foundation of civil law systems across much of Europe.

history.q: Which Bronze Age people built an empire in central Anatolia with its capital at Hattusa?
history.fact: The Hittite language is the oldest written Indo-European language known, recorded on clay tablets.

history.q: Which king of Lydia gave his name to a byword for great wealth?
history.fact: Croesus ruled from Sardis in western Anatolia until the Persian king Cyrus the Great conquered Lydia in the 6th century BCE.

history.q: Which 1071 battle, in which Alp Arslan captured a Byzantine emperor, opened Anatolia to the Seljuk Turks?
history.fact: Emperor Romanos IV Diogenes was captured at Manzikert (Malazgirt) and later released on ransom.

history.q: Which 1923 treaty set out the internationally recognised borders of the new Turkish state?
history.fact: The treaty was signed in Switzerland on 24 July 1923, a few months before the Republic was proclaimed.

history.q: At which 1402 battle was Ottoman sultan Bayezid I defeated and captured by Timur?
history.fact: Bayezid's defeat led to over a decade of civil war among his sons, known as the Ottoman Interregnum.

history.q: Which legendary king, whose touch supposedly turned things to gold, ruled Phrygia from Gordion?
history.fact: Alexander the Great is said to have cut the famous Gordian Knot at Gordion in 333 BCE.

history.q: Which elite Ottoman infantry corps was abolished by Sultan Mahmud II in 1826?
history.fact: The Janissaries' military band, the mehter, is considered one of the oldest military bands in the world.

history.q: Which Ottoman sultan conquered Mamluk Egypt in 1517?
history.fact: Selim's conquests of Syria, Egypt and western Arabia greatly enlarged the empire in a reign of just eight years.

history.q: Which city did the Ottomans capture in 1326 and make their first major capital?
history.fact: Bursa holds the tombs of the early sultans Osman and Orhan, and its silk trade made it wealthy.

history.q: Which Seljuk state had its capital at Konya in central Anatolia?
history.fact: "Rum" means "Rome," referring to the former Byzantine lands the Seljuks ruled in Anatolia.

history.q: Which Neolithic town in central Anatolia had houses so tightly packed that people entered them through the roof?
history.fact: Çatalhöyük was occupied from around 7400 BCE and its wall paintings include an early landscape scene.

history.q: Which 1699 treaty marked the first major Ottoman territorial losses in central Europe?
history.fact: The treaty, which ceded most of Hungary to the Habsburgs, followed the failed Ottoman siege of Vienna in 1683.

history.q: Which 1839 decree launched the Ottoman reform era known as the Tanzimat?
history.fact: Read aloud in the Gülhane rose garden of Topkapı Palace, it promised security of life, honour and property to all subjects.

history.q: In what year was the first Ottoman constitution proclaimed?
history.fact: Sultan Abdulhamid II suspended it in 1878; it was restored in 1908.

history.q: Herodotus, called the "Father of History", was born in which city on Anatolia's Aegean coast?
history.fact: Halicarnassus is today's resort town of Bodrum.

history.q: Which Hellenistic dynasty, whose last king bequeathed his realm to Rome in 133 BCE, ruled from Pergamon?
history.fact: Attalus III's will turned his kingdom into the Roman province of Asia.

technology.q: Which ancient Anatolian kingdom is credited with minting the first coins?
technology.fact: The earliest Lydian coins, from the 7th century BCE, were struck from electrum, a natural gold-silver alloy.

technology.q: Which writing material takes its name from the ancient Anatolian city of Pergamon?
technology.fact: Pergamon's library was said to rival Alexandria's, and its scribes became famous for writing on prepared animal skins.

technology.q: Which incendiary weapon helped the Byzantines defend Constantinople from naval attack?
technology.fact: Its recipe was such a closely guarded state secret that it is still not known for certain today.

technology.q: Turkey is the world's largest producer of which nut?
technology.fact: Most of the crop grows on the hillsides of the Black Sea coast, and much of it ends up in chocolate spreads.

technology.q: In which field did Turkish-born scientist Aziz Sancar win a Nobel Prize in 2015?
technology.fact: Sancar shared the prize for mapping how cells repair damaged DNA.

technology.q: In what year did the first bridge across the Bosphorus open?
technology.fact: It opened on 30 October 1973, a day after the Republic's 50th anniversary, linking Europe and Asia by road.

technology.q: Which Istanbul cistern, built under Justinian, has 336 columns and two carved Medusa heads?
technology.fact: The underground reservoir could hold around 80,000 cubic metres of water for the Great Palace and nearby buildings.

technology.q: Which dam on the Euphrates is Turkey's largest?
technology.fact: Built in the 1980s and early 1990s, it is the centrepiece of the Southeastern Anatolia Project for irrigation and hydropower.

technology.q: Which rail tunnel beneath the Bosphorus, opened in 2013, links the European and Asian sides of Istanbul?
technology.fact: Digging the tunnel uncovered the Byzantine harbour of Theodosius at Yenikapı, with dozens of ancient shipwrecks.

technology.q: Which cannon-maker cast giant bombards for Mehmed II's siege of Constantinople in 1453?
technology.fact: Orban had reportedly first offered his services to the Byzantines, who could not afford him.

technology.q: Which Ottoman admiral drew a world map in 1513 that shows part of the Americas?
technology.fact: The surviving fragment of the map, drawn on gazelle-skin parchment, was rediscovered at Topkapı Palace in 1929.

technology.q: Turkey holds most of the world's known reserves of which mineral, used in glass, ceramics and detergents?
technology.fact: Boron compounds are also used in fibreglass and heat-resistant borosilicate glass.

technology.q: Which home-appliance brand, sold widely across Europe, belongs to the Turkish company Arçelik?
technology.fact: Arçelik is part of Koç Holding, one of Turkey's largest industrial groups.

technology.q: Which Roman emperor's aqueduct still strides across central Istanbul?
technology.fact: Completed in 368 CE, the Valens Aqueduct carried water into Constantinople for well over a thousand years.

technology.q: Constantinople's massive land walls, which held for about a thousand years, are named after which emperor?
technology.fact: The walls combined a moat, an outer wall and a taller inner wall studded with nearly 100 towers.

technology.q: Turkey's first high-speed rail line, opened in 2009, linked Ankara with which city?
technology.fact: The line was later extended to Istanbul and Konya, cutting journey times dramatically.

technology.q: Turkey's first nuclear power plant, built with Russia's Rosatom, is at which Mediterranean site?
technology.fact: Akkuyu, in Mersin province, is designed with four reactors.

technology.q: Which philosopher from Miletus is said to have predicted the solar eclipse of 585 BCE?
technology.fact: According to Herodotus, the eclipse halted a battle between the Lydians and the Medes.

technology.q: Which Turkish mathematician, known for an "invariant" named after him, appears on the 10-lira banknote?
technology.fact: The Arf invariant from his 1941 paper is still used in topology and coding theory.

technology.q: Which Turkish surgeon was named "Neurosurgery's Man of the Century" for pioneering microneurosurgery?
technology.fact: Yaşargil developed many techniques and instruments for operating on the brain under a microscope.

technology.q: Which engineer at the Artuqid court in Diyarbakır wrote a famous 1206 book of ingenious mechanical devices?
technology.fact: His book describes water clocks, automata and pumps, illustrated with detailed drawings.

technology.q: Which mathematician from Tralles co-designed Hagia Sophia with Isidore of Miletus?
technology.fact: Their dome was so daring that it partly collapsed after an earthquake in 558 and had to be rebuilt higher.

technology.q: Who founded the first Ottoman printing press for books in Turkish, in the 1720s?
technology.fact: His first book, an Arabic-Turkish dictionary, appeared in 1729.

technology.q: Which astronomer built an observatory in Istanbul in 1577 that was demolished only a few years later?
technology.fact: The observatory was torn down in 1580, after the appearance of a great comet in 1577 had stirred controversy at court.

technology.q: Who designed and flew the first aircraft built in Turkey, the Vecihi K-VI, in 1925?
technology.fact: Hürkuş had been a fighter pilot in the First World War before turning to designing his own aircraft.

art.q: Which Istanbul monument was completed as a cathedral under Emperor Justinian in 537?
art.fact: Its 31-metre-wide dome seemed to float on a ring of windows, and it was the world's largest cathedral for nearly a thousand years.

art.q: Which Istanbul mosque is popularly called the "Blue Mosque" for its interior tiles?
art.fact: Completed in the early 1600s, it is unusual for having six minarets.

art.q: Which chief Ottoman architect designed the Süleymaniye Mosque in Istanbul and the Selimiye Mosque in Edirne?
art.fact: Sinan is credited with hundreds of buildings and called the Selimiye in Edirne his masterpiece.

art.q: Which Turkish novelist won the 2006 Nobel Prize in Literature?
art.fact: Pamuk opened a real Museum of Innocence in Istanbul to accompany his novel of the same name.

art.q: Which 13th-century Sufi poet, buried in Konya, inspired the order known for its whirling dervishes?
art.fact: Known in Turkey as Mevlana, Rumi wrote the Masnavi, a long spiritual poem in Persian.

art.q: Which Istanbul palace was the main residence of the Ottoman sultans for nearly 400 years?
art.fact: Topkapı is now a museum whose treasures include the 86-carat Spoonmaker's Diamond.

art.q: Which of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World stood at Halicarnassus, modern Bodrum?
art.fact: The tomb of Mausolus was so grand that "mausoleum" became the word for any monumental tomb.

art.q: Which of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World stood at Ephesus?
art.fact: Only a single re-erected column now marks the site of the once-vast temple.

art.q: Which Turkish TV drama about the life of Suleiman the Magnificent became an international hit in the early 2010s?
art.fact: "Muhteşem Yüzyıl" was broadcast in dozens of countries and boosted tourism to Topkapı Palace.

art.q: The reconstructed façade of the Library of Celsus stands in which ancient city?
art.fact: Built in the 2nd century CE, the library also served as a tomb for the Roman senator Celsus.

art.q: What is the Turkish art of making swirling patterns by floating paint on water and lifting them onto paper?
art.fact: Ebru, known in English as paper marbling, is on UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage.

art.q: Which 19th-century Bosphorus palace replaced Topkapı as the sultans' main residence?
art.fact: Atatürk died there on 10 November 1938, and the palace clocks are still set to 9:05, the time of his death.

art.q: Which modernist poet wrote the epic "Human Landscapes from My Country"?
art.fact: Nazım Hikmet wrote much of the work while in prison, and spent his last years in exile.

art.q: Which painter of "The Tortoise Trainer" (1906) also founded Istanbul's Archaeology Museum?
art.fact: The painting now hangs in Istanbul's Pera Museum, which bought it in 2004 for a record price.

art.q: The 16th-century glazed tiles decorating Topkapı Palace and the Blue Mosque were mainly made in which town?
art.fact: İznik potters perfected a vivid "tomato red" glaze that was famously hard to reproduce.

art.q: Which author wrote "Memed, My Hawk" (İnce Memed), about a bandit in the Taurus Mountains?
art.fact: Published in 1955, the novel has been translated into dozens of languages.

art.q: Nuri Bilge Ceylan won the Palme d'Or at Cannes in 2014 for which film?
choices: Once Upon a Time in Anatolia
art.fact: The three-hour drama is set in a cave hotel in snowy Cappadocia.

art.q: Which site near Şanlıurfa has carved T-shaped stone pillars more than 11,000 years old?
art.fact: Its monumental enclosures were built by hunter-gatherers, before the invention of pottery or writing.

art.q: Karagöz and Hacivat are the stock characters of which traditional Turkish art?
art.fact: Legend links the pair to builders of a Bursa mosque; their comic shadow plays are on UNESCO's intangible heritage list.

art.q: Which 13th-14th-century poet is celebrated for pioneering mystical poetry in everyday Turkish?
art.fact: Turkey's cultural institute abroad, the Yunus Emre Institute, is named after him.

art.q: Which 16th-century Ottoman polymath painted detailed bird's-eye views of cities on Suleiman's campaigns?
art.fact: Matrakçı Nasuh was also a mathematician and is credited with inventing the martial game of matrak.

art.q: Which ancient city in Caria, famed for its school of marble sculptors, was named after a goddess of love?
art.fact: Aphrodisias was added to the UNESCO World Heritage list in 2017.

art.q: Which composer, one of the "Turkish Five", wrote the oratorio "Yunus Emre" (1942)?
art.fact: Saygun also collaborated with Béla Bartók on folk-song research in Anatolia in 1936.

art.q: Which architect designed Anıtkabir, Atatürk's mausoleum in Ankara, together with Orhan Arda?
art.fact: Their design won an international competition in 1942, and the mausoleum was completed in 1953.

art.q: Which Turkish pianist composed "Black Earth", inspired by a song of the folk poet Âşık Veysel?
art.fact: Say imitates the sound of the bağlama, a Turkish long-necked lute, by muting the piano strings with his hand.

politics.q: What is the capital of Turkey?
politics.fact: Ankara became the capital in October 1923, replacing Istanbul, which had been the imperial seat for centuries.

politics.q: What is the name of Turkey's parliament?
politics.fact: Its full name is the Grand National Assembly of Turkey (Türkiye Büyük Millet Meclisi).

politics.q: In 1928, Turkey replaced the Arabic script for writing Turkish with which alphabet?
politics.fact: Atatürk toured the country with a blackboard and chalk to teach the new letters himself.

politics.q: Who served as Turkey's Prime Minister from 2003 to 2014 and then became President?
politics.fact: In 2014 he became the first Turkish president elected directly by popular vote.

politics.q: Which military alliance did Turkey join in 1952?
politics.fact: Turkey and Greece joined NATO together in February 1952, in the alliance's first enlargement.

politics.q: What does the surname "Atatürk" mean?
politics.fact: A 1934 law granted him the name and barred anyone else from adopting it.

politics.q: In 1945, Turkey was among the founding members of which organisation?
politics.fact: Turkey signed the UN Charter in San Francisco in June 1945.

politics.q: On which date does Turkey celebrate Republic Day?
politics.fact: Celebrations include flag-filled streets, parades and fireworks over the Bosphorus.

politics.q: Turkey applied to join the European Community in 1987 and began membership talks with which body in 2005?
politics.fact: Turkey has had a customs union with the EU since 1996.

politics.q: Who succeeded Atatürk as President of Turkey in 1938?
politics.fact: İnönü had been Atatürk's chief negotiator at Lausanne and served as president until 1950.

politics.q: In what year did the Turkish Grand National Assembly abolish the Ottoman sultanate?
politics.fact: The last sultan, Mehmed VI, left Istanbul aboard a British warship in November 1922.

politics.q: In what year did Turkish women gain the right to vote and stand in national elections?
politics.fact: Eighteen women were elected to parliament in the 1935 election that followed.

politics.q: A 2017 referendum approved Turkey's switch to which system of government?
politics.fact: The changes took full effect after the 2018 elections, abolishing the office of prime minister.

politics.q: Which office, held for centuries by Ottoman sultans, was abolished by Turkey's parliament in 1924?
politics.fact: The last caliph, Abdulmejid II, was also a painter whose works hang in Turkish museums.

politics.q: Which 1934 law required every citizen of Turkey to adopt a family surname?
politics.fact: Before the law, most Turks were known by a given name plus a nickname, title or father's name.

politics.q: Which party won Turkey's 1950 election, ending the Republican People's Party's long period in power?
politics.fact: Celal Bayar became president and Adnan Menderes prime minister after the vote.

politics.q: Which political party did Atatürk found in 1923?
politics.fact: Known by its Turkish initials CHP, it is the oldest political party in the Republic.

politics.q: Mustafa Kemal landed at which Black Sea port on 19 May 1919, a date taken as the start of the War of Independence?
politics.fact: 19 May is now Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day.

politics.q: Turkey's 1926 Civil Code was adapted from which country's code?
politics.fact: The new code banned polygamy and gave women equal rights in divorce and inheritance.

politics.q: Which movement's 1908 revolution forced the Ottoman sultan to restore the constitution?
politics.fact: Their Committee of Union and Progress went on to dominate Ottoman politics until 1918.

politics.q: Who became Turkey's first female Prime Minister, in 1993?
politics.fact: Çiller, an economist, led the True Path Party and served as prime minister until 1996.

politics.q: Which founder of the Motherland Party served as Prime Minister and then became President in 1989?
politics.fact: Özal's government opened up Turkey's economy to exports and foreign trade in the 1980s.

politics.q: In what year did the Grand National Assembly first convene in Ankara?
politics.fact: It opened on 23 April 1920, now celebrated as National Sovereignty and Children's Day.

politics.q: Which politician served as Prime Minister seven times before becoming President from 1993 to 2000?
politics.fact: Demirel, a trained engineer, was a leading figure in Turkish politics for four decades.

politics.q: Who was the last Grand Vizier of the Ottoman Empire?
politics.fact: His office ended along with the sultanate in November 1922.

current-affairs.q: On 6 February 2023, a devastating earthquake struck southern Turkey near which city?
current-affairs.fact: A second powerful quake struck the same region hours later, and the disaster affected eleven provinces.

current-affairs.q: In 2022, the United Nations agreed to Turkey's request to be known internationally by which name?
current-affairs.fact: The UN accepted the change in June 2022; Türkiye is how the country has long referred to itself in Turkish.

current-affairs.q: In July 2020, Istanbul's Hagia Sophia was reopened as what?
current-affairs.fact: It had served as a museum since 1934; visitors of all faiths can still enter outside prayer times.

current-affairs.q: Which city hosted the 2023 UEFA Champions League final?
current-affairs.fact: Manchester City beat Inter Milan 1-0 at the Atatürk Olympic Stadium on 10 June 2023.

current-affairs.q: Which Turkish electric-car brand began delivering its first model, the T10X, in 2023?
current-affairs.fact: Togg's factory is in Gemlik, near Bursa.

current-affairs.q: Which Turkish-born scientist co-founded BioNTech, whose COVID-19 vaccine with Pfizer was approved in 2020?
current-affairs.fact: Şahin, born in İskenderun, founded the company in Germany with his wife, Özlem Türeci.

current-affairs.q: Who won Turkey's presidential runoff election on 28 May 2023?
current-affairs.fact: It was the first presidential runoff in Turkey's history, held two weeks after the first round.

current-affairs.q: In 2023, Turkey's women's national team won both the Nations League and the European Championship in which sport?
current-affairs.fact: It was the first time the women's volleyball team had won the European title.

current-affairs.q: Which Turkish shooter went viral at the Paris 2024 Olympics for his relaxed, hand-in-pocket style while winning silver?
current-affairs.fact: Dikeç and Şevval İlayda Tarhan won silver in the mixed team 10 m air pistol event.

current-affairs.q: The Çanakkale 1915 Bridge, opened in March 2022, set a world record for what?
current-affairs.fact: Its main span is 2,023 m long, a nod to the Republic's centenary year.

current-affairs.q: In April 2019, Turkish Airlines moved its main hub from Atatürk Airport to which airport?
current-affairs.fact: The overnight move of equipment was one of the largest airport relocations ever attempted.

current-affairs.q: Who became the first Turkish astronaut to visit the International Space Station, in January 2024?
current-affairs.fact: Gezeravcı, an air force pilot, flew on the Axiom Mission 3 and carried out experiments in orbit.

current-affairs.q: Which round did Turkey's men's football team reach at Euro 2024?
current-affairs.fact: Turkey lost 2-1 to the Netherlands in Berlin after beating Austria in the round of 16.

current-affairs.q: Which Turkish midfielder joined Real Madrid from Fenerbahçe in July 2023?
current-affairs.fact: Güler was 18 when he signed; he scored a memorable long-range goal for Turkey at Euro 2024.

current-affairs.q: In 2021, Mete Gazoz won Turkey's first Olympic gold medal in which sport?
current-affairs.fact: Gazoz won the men's individual title at the Tokyo Games.

current-affairs.q: Which city, known in antiquity as Antioch, was heavily damaged in the February 2023 earthquakes?
current-affairs.fact: Antakya is famed for its mosaics museum, one of the largest collections of Roman mosaics in the world.

current-affairs.q: On 29 October 2023, Turkey marked the 100th anniversary of what?
choices: The adoption of the Latin alphabet
current-affairs.fact: Celebrations included a naval parade of ships on the Bosphorus and nationwide fireworks.

current-affairs.q: Which club won Turkey's Süper Lig in the 2023-24 season?
current-affairs.fact: Galatasaray finished with a club-record 102 points, just ahead of rivals Fenerbahçe.

current-affairs.q: Which Turkish actress won Best Actress at the Cannes Film Festival in 2023 for "About Dry Grasses"?
current-affairs.fact: The film was directed by Nuri Bilge Ceylan and is set in a village in eastern Anatolia.

current-affairs.q: Which club won the 2021-22 Süper Lig, its first league title since 1984?
current-affairs.fact: Trabzonspor was the first club from outside Istanbul to win the Turkish league, back in 1976.

current-affairs.q: Busenaz Sürmeneli won Olympic gold at the Tokyo Games in 2021 in which sport?
current-affairs.fact: She won the women's welterweight title, Turkey's first Olympic gold in women's boxing.

current-affairs.q: Which company's rocket launched Turkey's Türksat 5A communications satellite in January 2021?
current-affairs.fact: Türksat 5A rode a Falcon 9 from Cape Canaveral, Florida.

current-affairs.q: In 2021, the Sea of Marmara was coated with a thick layer of what, nicknamed "sea snot"?
current-affairs.fact: The slimy mucilage was linked to warm water and pollution; a large clean-up operation followed.

current-affairs.q: Alperen Şengün was named an NBA All-Star in 2025 while playing for which team?
current-affairs.fact: The Giresun-born centre joined Houston in 2021 and became only the second Turkish player to be named an NBA All-Star.

current-affairs.q: Which club won the 2019 UEFA Super Cup, played in Istanbul?
current-affairs.fact: Liverpool beat Chelsea on penalties at Beşiktaş's stadium in August 2019.

general.q: Which city straddles Europe and Asia on either side of the Bosphorus?
general.fact: Istanbul is the most populous city in Europe, with roughly 15 million residents.

general.q: What is Turkey's currency?
general.fact: The lira's symbol ₺ was introduced in 2012 and is based on the letter L with two strokes like an anchor.

general.q: Which central Anatolian region is famous for "fairy chimney" rock spires and sunrise hot-air balloon flights?
general.fact: People carved homes, churches and even entire underground cities into Cappadocia's soft volcanic rock.

general.q: Which site near Denizli is famous for its terraces of white travertine pools?
general.fact: Pamukkale means "cotton castle"; the ruins of the Roman spa city Hierapolis sit on top.

general.q: Which layered filo pastry with chopped nuts and syrup is one of Turkey's best-known desserts?
general.fact: Gaziantep is especially renowned for its pistachio baklava.

general.q: Which sea lies along Turkey's northern coast?
general.fact: The Black Sea coast is Turkey's rainiest region and its tea-growing heartland.

general.q: Which strait connects the Sea of Marmara to the Aegean Sea?
general.fact: In ancient times it was called the Hellespont, which the Persian king Xerxes crossed on a bridge of boats.

general.q: Which mountain, associated with Noah's Ark, is Turkey's highest peak?
general.fact: Ararat, called Ağrı Dağı in Turkish, is a dormant volcano rising to about 5,137 m.

general.q: Which Istanbul market, with around 4,000 shops, is one of the oldest and largest covered markets in the world?
general.fact: Construction of its core began in the 1450s soon after the Ottoman conquest of the city.

general.q: What is Turkey's largest lake?
general.fact: Lake Van is highly alkaline, and few fish other than the pearl mullet can live in it.

general.q: Edirne's Kırkpınar festival is famous for which sport?
general.fact: Wrestlers douse themselves in olive oil; the event is said to have been held since the 14th century.

general.q: Which sesame-crusted bread ring is sold from street carts all over Turkey?
general.fact: Simit is often eaten for breakfast with tea, cheese and olives.

general.q: Which mountain-top site features giant stone heads from the tomb-sanctuary of King Antiochus I of Commagene?
general.fact: Visitors climb before dawn to watch the sunrise light up the toppled heads of gods and kings.

general.q: The Tigris and which other great river both rise in the mountains of eastern Turkey?
general.fact: The two rivers flow south to Mesopotamia, the "land between the rivers."

general.q: What is the blue glass eye charm, believed to ward off the evil eye, called in Turkish?
general.fact: Nazar charms hang everywhere from cars and doorways to babies' clothes.

general.q: Which Aegean port is Turkey's third-largest city?
general.fact: Izmir was known in antiquity as Smyrna, and it is one of the claimed birthplaces of Homer.

general.q: Which aniseed-flavoured spirit, turning milky white with water, is nicknamed "lion's milk" in Turkey?
general.fact: Rakı is traditionally sipped slowly with meze and fish.

general.q: In 2000, which Istanbul club became the first Turkish team to win a European trophy, the UEFA Cup?
general.fact: Galatasaray beat Arsenal on penalties in Copenhagen, then won the UEFA Super Cup against Real Madrid.

general.q: Which energetic folk dance, performed in a line with shoulders shimmying, comes from Turkey's Black Sea region?
general.fact: Horon is often danced to the kemençe, a small bowed fiddle of the Black Sea coast.

general.q: Which shallow salt lake in central Anatolia is Turkey's second-largest lake?
general.fact: Lake Tuz supplies a large share of Turkey's salt and turns pink in summer, attracting flamingos.

general.q: Which lake in southwest Turkey, nicknamed "Turkey's Maldives", was studied by NASA as a model of a Martian crater?
general.fact: Salda's white shores are made of minerals similar to those in Jezero Crater, where the Perseverance rover landed.

general.q: What is the longest river flowing entirely within Turkey?
general.fact: Its name means "Red River" in Turkish, from the reddish sediment it carries; it was the Halys of antiquity.

general.q: The Kangal shepherd dog is named after a district in which Turkish province?
general.fact: Kangals have guarded sheep from wolves for centuries and are prized for their calm, loyal temperament.

general.q: Which mountain near Bursa, known in antiquity as the Mysian Olympus, is a major ski resort?
general.fact: A cable car climbs from Bursa's city edge onto the mountain's slopes.

general.q: The Lycian Way, a long-distance hiking trail along the Mediterranean coast, runs from Fethiye to near which city?
general.fact: The waymarked route passes rock-cut tombs, ancient cities and beaches over roughly 500 km.
